decision: OM umbrella name remains OpenMessenger / OwnMessenger / OurMessenger (OM).
No infrastructure provider is part of the protocol; providers are plugins.
Normal identity is passwordless-by-default and device-first.
Phone numbers, usernames, emails and domains are aliases/claims, not root identity.
PersonRecord is local/private human contact state; no global authority merges humans.
Unknown senders use constrained MessageRequests/IntroductionEndpoints.
No global trust score or transitive Web of Trust.
Businesses use OrganizationIdentity + stable ServiceIdentity + scoped bot/human AgentAuthorization.
Private groups use AccountID membership and DeviceIdentity cryptographic membership; design around MLS.
Hot/cold/recovery storage classes are separate and can use different providers.
StoragePool supports provider selection and mirroring; erasure coding deferred.
Official app is a reference client; third-party clients/UIs use public protocol and conformance.
PWA is first execution path; web-first is not web-only.
Canonical conversation semantics use a small immutable event model with materialized views.
Authoritative identity/group control state is separate from chat content events.
Baseline durable events are message.create/edit/delete, reaction.set, receipt.update.
Baseline durable event size ceiling is 64 KiB; media is out-of-band encrypted blob storage.
Use client-generated random EventIDs and Hybrid Logical Clock ordering; no central sequencer.
Authority must be scoped, replaceable, and non-composable; OM requires no universal central authority.
AccountID is algorithm-independent and must not be used as a relay/media routing address.
Wire cryptography negotiates approved versioned CryptoProfiles, not arbitrary primitive combinations.
Crypto upgrades are automatic/invisible for ordinary users and advance authenticated downgrade floors.
OM prefers PQ-first/hybrid-secure profiles where mature; draft-dependent suites remain replaceable.
Accepted relationships use private rotatable opaque delivery capabilities; relays need not know stable AccountIDs.
Voice/video media uses route-independent SFrame E2EE; signaling is encrypted OM control traffic.
Call RoutePolicy prefers safe LAN/direct P2P when policy permits, then TURN fallback; SFU is used for scalable groups.
Cloudflare is an optional reference relay/blob/media deployment, never a protocol dependency.
R2 is one possible encrypted BlobStore; delivery queues and archives remain separate storage classes.
SMS/MMS/RCS are deferred from initial implementation but preserved as future TransportAdapters.
Provider routing is budget/quota-aware; a zero-paid-budget policy must be enforceable.
OM is local-first and should support privacy-preserving LAN direct messaging/files/calls where feasible.
Abuse controls use first-contact/recipient/group/provider/reporting boundaries without universal content surveillance or mandatory global trust score.
OM discovery is a resolver fabric, not a mandatory global registry; every discovery method yields a validated ContactDescriptor.
Bare usernames retain namespace/provider provenance; OM has no protocol-global bare username root or mandatory blockchain ledger.
Public directory records expose IntroductionServiceDescriptor data, not reusable private relationship mailbox capabilities.
QR/link invitations are independently revocable, expiring, scoped capabilities; revocation does not affect accepted relationships.
IntroGate issues short-lived/single-use IntroductionTickets and enforces first-contact abuse/resource policy without ambient conversation plaintext.
Directory lookup should support optional oblivious relay/resolver separation so one party need not learn both requester IP and queried alias.
Multiple simultaneous relays are first-class through a private authenticated RelaySet with distinct capability per relay and automatic failover.
LAN discovery uses rotating rendezvous tokens derived from purpose-specific relationship/invite secrets rather than stable identity broadcast.
OM designs for censorship resilience through provider and transport diversity/pluggable transports but makes no guarantee of uncensorability.
Recovery is optional and off by default; a user may intentionally have an unrecoverable/disposable AccountID.
Identity recovery, history decryption recovery, and provider recovery are separate authorities and key hierarchies.
Account authority uses monotonic authenticated AccountControlState rather than chat-event HLC or last-write-wins.
Device compromise response separates immediate quarantine from permanent revocation; quarantine cannot shrink its own constitutional quorum.
Control-device promotion is a constitutional operation authorized by the pre-change control set or RecoveryPolicy.
AccountControlHead gossip/witness observations detect rollback/forks but cannot author successor control state.
Initial personal deployments are user-owned Cloudflare accounts; the official app may automate provisioning but Cloudflare remains replaceable.
workers.dev FQDNs are valid v1 personal discovery locators/aliases; organizations/FQDN owners are the first natural grouped directories.
Contact sharing uses subject-signed expiring ContactCapsules; introducers may add referral context but are not identity authorities.
Zero-payment reference Cloudflare core is Worker + SQLite Durable Object; R2/D1/Pages are optional capabilities.
Software-update trust starts with signed/mirrored source, TUF-style role separation, provenance, pinning and reproducibility where feasible.
Security/privacy profiles change metadata/convenience policies but never reduce the strongest approved compatible cryptographic floor.
Push providers receive only opaque wake information; local clients fetch/decrypt/render notification content. Vendor push may be disabled with explicit delivery tradeoffs.
Backups can restore history but cannot restore stale account authority; current AccountControlState must be reconciled before full operation.
OM v1 does not upload or hash the user's address book; local Contacts permission is display/convenience only.
Disappearing-message lifecycle is client-enforced and backup-aware; view-once is never backed up and expired content is never restored.
Protocol extensions have explicit critical/non-critical semantics and authenticated capability negotiation before wire freeze.
Endpoint-assurance classes and nation-state anonymity transports remain pluggable future policy/capability layers rather than v1 blockers.
OM Protocol/Core requires no OM-operated account, relay, directory, push, recovery, or abuse service for established communication.
The first reference client is PWA-first but native Android/iOS shells remain planned; PWA is not a permanent capability ceiling.
Security/state semantics should converge on one portable memory-safe OM Core shared by WASM and native shells.
Provisioning is replaceable; provider-native deploy templates are preferred where they avoid an OM-controlled provisioning service, while OAuth remains optional.
Operatorless-core abuse response is local blocking plus selective EvidencePackage export to a user-chosen recipient; no central OM AbuseDesk is required.
Push/signing/store-policy/reporting infrastructure for a native client is owned by that client distribution, not by the OM protocol.
Future convenience businesses/providers may exist but receive no protocol privilege and must preserve provider migration/identity continuity.
Creator-Disappearance Gate requires established independent users to continue communicating if the original project/author/business disappears.
Official reference clients share one om-ui implementation above om-core; platform shells provide OS capabilities/system surfaces rather than independent product semantics.
Reference layout adapts to actual window size through Compact/Medium/Expanded/Wide modes rather than device-specific application forks.
OM defines a semantic, interruptible MotionSystem and treats perceived smoothness as input latency, layout stability, local-first rendering and motion together.
OwnMessenger themes are declarative data-only bundles; no theme code execution, arbitrary remote assets, protocol hooks or security-semantic overrides are permitted.
PlatformAdapter exposes capabilities such as secure storage, push, system calls, files/share, local contacts and background execution without owning protocol/business logic.
Security-critical UI semantics, accessible focus and external-link meaning are protected from theme override.
Accessibility is implemented in shared UI primitives and treated as a release gate; WCAG 2.2 AA is the minimum shared-web baseline.
Default OM appearance prioritizes ergonomics/functionality, immediate legibility, calm content-first hierarchy and restrained aesthetics; personalization is optional.
PWA ClientHost/origin and IdentityHome are separate concepts; origin/provider migration uses authenticated new-device transfer and DeviceVault re-wrapping, not raw browser database copying.
Core/local storage is IdentityProfile-isolated from v1 even though visible multi-account switching ships later; no hidden global identifier links profiles.
Rich messages use bounded semantic RichTextV1 rather than HTML/CSS/JavaScript or Markdown as authoritative wire content.
Decrypted files, links, formatted clipboard input and themes remain hostile input and pass bounded validation/sandboxed rendering.
Ordinary message authenticity remains session/group-protocol based and does not add a durable AccountID signature solely for non-repudiation/evidence.
Local data receives explicit lifecycle classes and default diagnostics remain local/redacted/user-exported.
Canonical signed/wire objects use a strict OM deterministic-CBOR profile derived from RFC 8949.
AccountControlState TLA+ model checking is required before production control-authority implementation is accepted.
Engineering may use a clearly dev-only CryptoProvider, but production security claims are blocked until the production crypto integration gate passes.
Every accepted theme has safe light+dark variants and Auto follows system appearance; profile-specific theme suggestions are optional local UX.
The 14:34 engineering transition is superseded; OM remains architecture_hardening_pre_engineering and product engineering is unauthorized until a later architecture-freeze ADR.

OM uses a layered anti-capture licensing model: MPL-2.0 shared core, AGPL-3.0-or-later reference network services, Apache-2.0 normative protocol/conformance artifacts, CC-BY-SA-4.0 documentation, with DCO/inbound-equals-outbound contributions and no ordinary broad copyright assignment.
SeedLife/lonunjie is initial steward; founder-only S0 project custody is accepted until trustworthy maintainers emerge, while succession roles/key/asset migration rails are designed now.
Asynchronous per-device handshake material and MLS KeyPackage publication is a first-class replaceable KeyMaterialProvider role; consumable one-time items default to disjoint provider pools.
One-to-one multi-device session management is a distinct state machine above handshake/ratchet and validates device eligibility from AccountControlState.
MLS group architecture requires an application-level same-epoch Commit ordering/conflict profile and atomic/authenticated binding between OM group-control transitions and resulting MLS epochs.
Relay migration and blob relocation have explicit repair semantics: RelaySet continuity/overlap plus optional catastrophic rendezvous; stable BlobID with authenticated mutable BlobLocationRecord.
Every canonical time/TTL field declares a clock class; HLC and wall-clock values never authorize constitutional security state.
Self-hosted PWA ClientHosts require a release/deployment/update/rollback/compromised-origin migration lifecycle separate from DeviceVault identity continuity.
The architecture repository is governed by machine-readable phase/file/domain contracts and an executable drift validator; engineering_authorized remains false in this checkpoint.

OM intentionally carries seven canonical meanings: Open-source Messenger, OpenMessenger, OwnMessenger, OurMessenger, OneMessenger, OhMessenger and 0M (zero total control); all seven constrain product architecture.

Former Q-001..Q-061 architectural choices are resolved by ARCHITECTURE_RESOLUTIONS_20260923.md; remaining uncertainty is typed as architecture verification, public-release gates, deferred product measurements, or new architecture-design queue items.
No country is an OM protocol home jurisdiction; legal/compliance review is role-based and jurisdiction-specific only for the project-controlled distribution/service actually offered.

OM minimizes project legal exposure through standard open-source warranty/liability terms, minimal centralized custody/operation, and explicit operator boundaries; it does not use field-of-use restrictions or claim legal immunity.

Capability support does not imply SeedLife operation: OM may interoperate with content packs, bots, communities, broadcasts, catalogs, entitlements and future commerce providers without running those services.
Expressive media, community/broadcast, bot/LLM and plugin questions are architecture-design work that must be resolved before engineering because they affect event/control/extension surfaces.

The provisional product baseline includes first-class stickers and GIF-like looping animation, external portable content packs, and familiar messenger ergonomics; exact formats/security manifests remain architecture queue work.

OM Core does not issue a token, process payments, custody funds or act as merchant-of-record; any future paid-content capability must keep settlement/marketplace operation in an optional external provider/plugin role.

Independent OM clients are first-class OpenMessenger participants. Bots/LLMs/bridges are explicit principals with scoped access; a bridge or full-room bot that receives plaintext is a visible E2EE trust boundary.

Communities/spaces, room/channel types and broadcast publication are intended capabilities, but the exact composable control/membership model remains pre-engineering architecture work rather than being forced into the existing private-group model.

ConversationID is the single provider-independent wire identity of an interactive Room/private group; the former distinct GroupID is removed from current architecture, while SpaceID and PublicationID remain distinct object identities.

A Community is presented from a Space that links independent Rooms/Publications/nested Spaces. Space membership/linking does not silently create Room membership or MLS membership; official child affiliation is bilateral and delegated Room authority is explicit.

Room/Space authority is capability-scoped: roles are grant bundles, explicit restrictions subtract authority, delegation ceilings prevent self-escalation, high-risk transitions may require quorum, and no permanent owner or unrestricted Administrator bypass is protocol-required.

Replies and lightweight threads remain inside one ConversationID; persistent Topics are room-local organization. Private announcements are restricted-post MLS Rooms, while public broadcast uses separately signed Publication objects with non-canonical follower lists.

The V1 ordinary-messenger baseline has explicit semantic boundaries: shared pins/polls/moderation are interoperable state, voice notes are typed attachments, forwarding is new authorship, scheduling/search/drafts/mute/archive remain local/account-private, and calls remain separate session state.

Baseline expressive media is bounded inert WebP under semantic sticker/custom-emoji/reaction/loop kinds; sent conversation assets are immutable BlobID-addressed and do not depend on a live source pack/catalog.

Portable ContentPacks are data-only stable PackIDs with immutable canonical releases and signed update lineage; direct hosting/install/fork is first-class and provenance is not copyright/safety endorsement.

OM standardizes an optional generic entitlement-presentation boundary for pack acquisition/update while leaving payments, settlement, pricing, tax, refunds and marketplaces outside OM Core; already-delivered conversation content remains renderable without entitlement.

Bots, agents and LLMs use typed ServicePrincipals with separately governed endpoints; selected-context invocation is default, full-Room service membership is an explicit visible plaintext-recipient boundary, and local/network/tool capabilities remain separate.

OM separates protocol extensions, inert content, sandboxed local plugins, isolated web apps, remote services and provider adapters; official-client executable plugins use a capability-scoped WebAssembly Component Model/WIT host and cannot carry hidden canonical protocol meaning.

0M is a canonical secondary reading of OM: zero parties have total control. Decentralization is required at the level of ultimate authority/survivability, without pretending that every scoped service or deployment must itself be fully decentralized.

Service identity creation is local and permissionless; hosting/discovery/catalogs are optional replaceable roles. OM classifies authorship by authority rather than human/AI inference, and autonomous personal representation uses a scoped RepresentationGrant while remaining ServicePrincipal-authored.

External networks interoperate through typed BridgePrincipals whose foreign actor/event attribution remains explicit provenance; private-Room plaintext export and the OM-E2EE termination point are visible state, with capability/fidelity and loop semantics explicit.

OM Portable Archive v1 preserves portable history/evidence independently of clients/providers but never restores authority by itself; foreign imports remain non-routable provenance-bearing historical records rather than fabricated native OM history.

Metadata privacy is surface-specific: stable canonical identities are not default provider-routing identifiers, private delivery hides inner protocol identifiers behind scoped opaque capabilities/randomized outer envelopes, and E2EE is never presented as a blanket claim about timing/size/IP/membership metadata.

Abuse/moderation authority remains user/Room/Space/provider scoped. Optional signed SafetyAdvisories are composable policy inputs selected by subscribers, not protocol truth; OM has no mandatory global reputation score, master blocklist or universal moderator.

Protocol longevity uses mirrorable self-contained Protocol Continuity Bundles, immutable assigned registry meanings, explicit protocol/fork lineages and provider/distribution independence; market dominance or proprietary extensions do not acquire canonical protocol authority.

A-001 through A-015 are resolved at design level. OM remains architecture_hardening_pre_engineering with engineering_authorized=false until all blocking verification gates pass and a later ADR explicitly authorizes engineering.

Homes have tiers T0 sponsored starter mailbox, T1 hosted, T2 own cloud, T3 self-hosted, T4 local; none is protocol-privileged; T0 is the default first-run path from an invite; vendor monoculture is a declared 0M risk requiring a second non-cloud reference provider before public production.

Coercive/proximate adversaries and platform leakage are first-class threats; device enrollment is never silent; OM offers lock/quick-lock/travel posture but no hidden-volume deniability promise; LocalDataClass maps to per-platform leakage controls.

Vulnerability response is decentralized: distribution security contacts, steward-coordinated embargoes as a replaceable role, signed SecurityAdvisories as subscriber inputs, peer-local floors; no remote kill switch.

AccountRetirement is a terminal constitutional transition; deletion is retirement plus local wipe and Home purge; optional LegacyPolicy may only retire, memorialize and point to a pre-designated successor, cancellable by any live controller.
Core computes a local ContinuityAssessment; recovery stays off by default but is informed-off with a persistent non-blocking continuity check for single-point-of-loss configurations.
superseded_in_part: 'recovery stays off by default' is superseded by ADR-0111 (identity recovery on by default, one vote with delay and veto); the ContinuityAssessment part stands (ADR-0130 rule 12).

decision: PQ status is per conversation type: v1 1:1 is hybrid-PQ, v1 MLS groups/group calls are classical and must not be claimed PQ; group wire carries a tested ReInit path and migrates on objective adoption triggers.

V1 is a semantic contract delivered in waves W0..W4; engineering unlock is scope-granular via engineering_scopes, all unauthorized until an ADR names a scope whose gates passed pre-engineering criteria.

Gates carry pre-engineering/pre-release criteria, independence levels and unlock scopes; same-author evidence cannot pass a gate; requirements are fully traced and threats are kept in a validator-checked register.
The lonunjie/om git repository is canonical; prior checkpoints are tagged commits; zips are transport via tools/om_drop.py export/import with base-commit merge.

Identity recovery is on by default with an automatically chosen custodian (synced passkey PRF, else recovery key); activation alone waits >=24h (default 72h) with veto by any live controller, is immediate with >=1 controller co-sign, and the RecoveryRoot counts as one vote.
Cloudflare Worker+SQLite DO is the first T1 hosted-Home reference, multi-tenant from W0; T1 hosts do not serve members' ClientHost by default; community-hosted Homes are the growth path.
The whole system is designed before W0 engineering; later-wave gates with W0 interface impact need recorded feasibility evidence before W0 unlock.
Co-stewards are recruited from the early community; not a W0/first-release blocker; S2 claims still need multi-party custody; continuity bundle and disappearance drill compensate.
Measurable performance budgets are verification gate V-022 on reference_client_ui and provider_reference.
Verification CI runs validator, docs check, evidence and TLC with a digest-pinned tla2tools.jar; regenerated evidence must match committed results.

A cross-vendor AI agent review satisfies independent_reviewer for pre-engineering phases only, recorded in verification/reviews/; Claude-authored prototypes need a non-Anthropic reviewer; pre-release and external_review always need humans.

OM-Crypto-v1 is PQXDH + Double Ratchet (no SPQR: only implementation is AGPL); clean-room SPQR/ML-KEM Braid is the planned OM-Crypto-v2 path; permissive primitive crates plus OM-maintained composition; OM owns the wire/state contract.
W0 CDDL (18 objects) and six registries are frozen; 'reserved...' crypto constructions may be filled once when A-023..A-028 resolve; eight encoding contradictions ruled.
Session manager rules K1-K11 are normative (V-003 vectors are conformance tests); downgrade floor survives restore with authenticated below-floor reject; lazy session repair accepted.

Events authorized at sending epoch; LWW registers epoch-major; past_epoch_window GroupProfile parameter (default 2); equivocation rejects all versions; target-kind rules; kind-to-capability table; poll/topic rules.

Authority-reducing transitions are never forks and survive freezes (not AccountControlState); grants cascade with their basis; sub-delegation opt-in; unlink ends binding; services cannot be controllers; anti-rollback; moderating governance is constitutional; timeout ends by committed transition.
Evidence encrypted to the moderator set at report epoch, no clawback; appeal hold capped at hold_max (max 180 days past retention expiry).

Service triggers are disclosures; tainted invocations get no egress without plaintext_egress; bridge origin fingerprints Room-scoped; origin_unverified flag; bridge-to-bridge relay opt-in; no retroactive bridge export.

Archive manifest is canonical CBOR; manifest fields per spec §5; link_evidence or provenance downgrade; secret object type registry; OMA-ENC-1-candidate provisional; newer archived control state re-validated live.

W0 spec addendum: RequestKey, MessageRequest (HPKE base mode, hybrid KEM), MessageRequestPayload, IntroIdentityBinding (types 19-21); om.acs.fork_ack extension; security_generation per conversation type in crypto profiles; pq_signed_prekey mandatory; RelaySet semantics on frozen fields; ConversationEvent.expiry is the v1 timer; KMP descriptor corrected.

Account authority transition rules: recovery is one vote with delay and veto everywhere; normative per-delta authorization table; AccountRetirement(moved) is the only continuity proof; fork bridge via om.acs.fork_ack with device-only majority; LegacyPolicy authorization deferred to W1 (A-030).
amendment_note: ADR-0147 specifies crash/reboot persistence for verifier-local recovery delay as a conservative durable monotonic elapsed lower bound that wall time or restored historical state cannot accelerate.

decision: Group reductions live after sequencing_timeout with deterministic coordinator succession; account-control events in groups; MLS groups are transferably authenticated; HistoryBundle attributed to its author; invite-accept-add consent; opaque join_ref invites with issuer cascade; per-recipient wrapping, random group_id; CryptoProfile not governable; om-room-capabilities registry; role edits are grants; SpaceDelegatedIntent; ModerationDecision is a record, committed lifts; Publication seq chain; participant-bound call keys (isolation A-035); unknown callers do not ring; one expiry rule; epoch-major reactions/votes; W0-safe later-wave content; honest safety refs; mentions stay in the Room; naming.
superseded_in_part: ADR-0128 group-call MLS-exporter-only isolation text was replaced by participant-only per-sender SFrame key delivery in ADR-0132.
amendment_note: ADR-0150 supersedes ADR-0128’s list-block later-wave disposition by standardizing bounded non-critical om.rich-list.v1 presentation over W0-valid paragraph blocks; the frozen W0 RichText grammar is unchanged. ADR-0157 names the interoperable group artifact GroupHistoryBundle and distinguishes it from implementation-private DeviceHistorySnapshot.

decision: No autonomous Account-authored events from extension code; ADR-0124 taint covers every executable extension (1:1 plaintext_egress needs both participants); services and bridges are invocation-only or full members (subscription is a trigger filter; bridges always full); RepresentationGrants issued by a control device with cascading basis and counterparty notice; revoked service endpoints removed from Rooms with ADR-0128 liveness; personal grants notify other devices; PWA extensions on a separate site; owner-pinned ClientHost release root with transparency-before-deploy; shared ClientHost is a named non-privileged role; per-profile push registrations; vault wrapping separate from recovery custodian; built-in fonts on reserved surfaces; ExpressiveAssetRef is an attachment-ref; export honours expiry; DeviceVault labels implementation-private.

T0 client never served by the sponsor by default (native + two independent origins); every provisioning path activates a verified release (verifier-first templates, honest OAuth scopes); advisory key delegated from the TUF root, peer floors need the root threshold, expire and allow override; same-operator roles collude by construction; V-023 ClientHost update lifecycle gate and transparency roles; NetworkTransport contract and censorship claim discipline; machine-applicable PR gates and one S0 custody statement; LAN opt-in, fixed-cardinality; 30-day sponsor revocation overlap; conformance-suite registry; Home API (A-045) before provider_reference; stale text corrected.

Core-kernel final hardening: dual Ed25519+ML-DSA binding of PQXDH identity/prekeys; exact durable per-prekey replay ledger with fail-closed cap; AES-256-GCM-SIV DR payload profile; v1 header exposure explicit; exact PQ UI wording; verifier-local recovery observation delay; incarnation-bound rebasable reductions; symmetric IntroIdentityBinding; MessageRequest pins draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05 MLKEM768-X25519/HKDF-SHA256/ChaCha20Poly1305.
amendment_note: ADR-0147 specifies crash/reboot persistence for verifier-local recovery delay as a conservative durable monotonic elapsed lower bound that wall time or restored historical state cannot accelerate.

decision: Referral admission uses RFC 9578 publicly verifiable Blind-RSA tokens; group-call media keys are per-sender SFrame keys pairwise-distributed only to joined devices; remote mini-app plaintext crossing is itself egress; continuous 1:1 plaintext egress requires signed bilateral RelationshipPolicyConsent.

Home API and typed error registry are frozen as vendor-neutral capability APIs; ProviderCapabilities becomes real JSON Schema with durability_class; release transparency uses Rekor-v2/C2SP-style append-only checkpoints plus two independent signed monitor observations; all W0 conformance suites gain concrete case lists.

Verification execution is phase-separated and no-bounce: design closure, repo-local pre-engineering evidence, post-scope implementation evidence, and genuinely external evidence are distinct; interface-impact gates have explicit feasibility_criteria; verification prototypes are non-production; one executor completes all repo-local work before batched independent review; canonical unfinished work is derived from gate criteria, not free-text remaining notes.

OM-Crypto-v1 bytes are pinned inside the frozen W0 CDDL: composite Ed25519||ML-DSA-65 key (1984 B) and signature (3373 B) with exactly one device signature entry; PQXDH binding is the ACS -> DeviceCredential -> signed AsyncKeyBundle / signed prekey-item chain; handshake_id transcript and ledger applicability; DR header, header hash (new label OM-DR-HEADER-HASH-v1), K/N and AEAD AD; MessageRequest HPKE info; v1 dependency set without spqr/libsignal. Independent (non-Anthropic) review pending.

core_kernel review remediation (gpt-5.6-sol F-1..F-9): recovery method count never changes veto authority; threshold-disabling quarantine freezes and is resolved by a device-only majority counting quarantined controllers' challenge signatures; lift-quarantine rule is state-derived; responder binds IK_A to exactly one active committed DeviceCredential of the relationship peer before any secret-key operation (K12); stable_device_correlator declared for KeyMaterialProvider, mailbox-class Homes and push provider; referral tokens use exact RFC 9578 type 0x0002 (48-byte salt PSS, id-RSASSA-PSS SPKI key id) with issuance evidenced separately; continuity bundle has an explicit normative manifest. Re-review pending.

Security-boundary hardening: one machine-readable ACS transition policy; selective safety-freeze restoration only when every restored controller challenge-signs and the child regains the parent majority; mandatory RelationshipContext for every inbound 1:1 decrypt; authentication-layer metadata is modeled; W0 referral issuance requires fresh independent Blind-RSA blinding factors and issuer-to-redemption unlinkability; provider interfaces declare negative capabilities. Cross-model accepted-set equivalence is a separate independent follow-up and is not claimed here.

Design closure set 1: LegacyPolicy uses a preserved key-23 commitment plus verifier-local inactivity/contest and terminally narrow guardian authority; W0 AsyncKeyBundle linkage is accepted while v2 validates devices at relationship-pinned clients without account-wide ACS fields; group deniability is a v1 non-goal; sealed sender is a later outer-delivery CryptoProfile; routine provider administration uses opaque resource capabilities rather than DeviceCredential/ACS auth; RecoveryRecord gains opaque RecoveryRoot-derived read/write capability access and explicit get semantics while mailbox recovery fan-out leakage is declared.
superseded_in_part: The defer-to-v2 AsyncKeyBundle privacy cut was superseded by ADR-0140; LegacyPolicy criticality was corrected by ADR-0141; the later-profile sealed-sender disposition was superseded by ADR-0142, which makes sealed delivery mandatory for established OM-Crypto-v1 relay delivery.

decision: Final design closure: frozen W0 CDDL/registries/domain-separation rules outrank logical modeling schemas for wire bytes; SecurityAdvisory expiry/supersession/override can remove only an advisory-added floor and never lower the stored relationship security floor; historical open/TBD language is dispositioned; OMA-ENC-1-candidate is verification-only pending V-014 freeze; security invariants gain machine traceability; the 11-scope adversarial pass closes architecture but does not pass implementation gates or authorize engineering.

AsyncKeyBundle v1 is re-frozen without provider-visible ACS generation/hash; retired numeric keys 3/4 remain reserved. Signed-prekey generation is globally monotonic per DeviceID+CryptoProfile across provider pools with a durable recipient high-water mark and equal-generation core-hash equivocation check. One-time prekeys are signed over DeviceID/profile/generation/provider_pool_id/kind/key_id/public_key. Provider revokeGeneration is operational only; restore and compromise semantics are explicit.

Semantic consistency remediation: om.acs.legacy_policy is critical/fail-closed; provider bearer capabilities receive normative transport/redaction/no-store rules; RecoveryRecord v1 has authenticated monotonic freshness and last-known ACS observation with stale-snapshot revalidation; RecoveryRoot metadata-confidentiality limits and optional Maximum-Privacy split relationship custody are explicit; W0 domain labels and the 300-second default skew are frozen; stale A-035 call-key text is amended to ADR-0132 participant-only SFrame key delivery.

Run-3 sealed delivery is promoted into pre-release OM-Crypto-v1 for established 1:1 mailbox/relay delivery. The complete ordinary envelope is HPKE-wrapped with profile-pinned PQ/T HPKE and simple size buckets; per-relationship/per-device/per-route signed delivery-key records avoid RelaySet size blow-up; MessageRequest carries a request-scoped acceptance-reply bootstrap key; durable replay/expiry, route binding, multi-device/rotation and explicit no-clear-fallback rules are normative; outer open never replaces inner RelationshipContext/sender authentication.
amendment_note: ADR-0143 refines durable replay into crash-safe RESERVED/COMPLETE/REJECTED; ADR-0144 scopes the MessageRequest bootstrap key and composes RESERVED with stale-ACS refresh; ADR-0145 closes the bootstrap to exactly one logical response and makes existing COMPLETE exact-retry lookup precede live key lookup; ADR-0146 atomically terminalizes losing RESERVED candidates, clarifies bounded reply-route transport use and binds wrapper expiry to key/route/request acceptance. ADR-0147 derives the bootstrap deadline from signed route/key expiry, makes candidate accounting non-replenishable, pins replay-only expiry/GC and forbids historical restore of live bootstrap state.

decision: Sealed-delivery replay persistence is crash-safe: a durable replay record distinguishes RESERVED, COMPLETE and REJECTED and binds the exact wrapper fingerprint. An exact same-route/same-wrapper retry may resume RESERVED after crash; COMPLETE is idempotent and never repeats inner effects; a different wrapper under the same key/id is rejected. Inner K2 session/dedupe acceptance and COMPLETE commit crash-consistently before application release/ack. No wire object, provider authority or crypto primitive changes.
amendment_note: ADR-0144 keeps stale-ACS-indeterminate authentication RESERVED; ADR-0145 permits an existing exact COMPLETE replay to be recognized/acknowledged before live delivery-key lookup, while RESERVED exact retries still require retained key material.

decision: Final pre-review sealed-delivery semantic closure: MessageRequest reply_delivery_key is fresh and durably scoped to one pending request/profile/exact reply route with bounded expiry/disposal and no authority promotion; a RESERVED wrapper whose inner authentication is undecidable only because trusted peer ACS may be stale remains RESERVED with no release/ack until authenticated monotonic refresh yields a definitive accept/reject result. V-003 gains a separate local-evidence criterion for these composition negatives before different-vendor review.
amendment_note: ADR-0145 removes the remaining bootstrap-lifecycle ambiguity: one logical response wins atomically, completed retries use replay-only state before key lookup, and bootstrap completion/import/request closure is crash-consistent. ADR-0147 derives the bootstrap deadline from signed route/key expiry, makes candidate accounting non-replenishable, pins replay-only expiry/GC and forbids historical restore of live bootstrap state.

decision: Final bootstrap retry/race closure: each MessageRequest accepts at most one logical bootstrap response. The first valid requester-side crash-consistent commit atomically binds the winning exact wrapper, authenticated recipient binding/imported established delivery state, inner dedupe/COMPLETE and request closure to COMPLETE_REPLAY_ONLY. Existing exact COMPLETE retries are recognized from durable replay metadata before live key lookup/HPKE so the completed bootstrap private key may be destroyed without losing a lost-ack retry; RESERVED retains key material needed to resume. Different wrappers and losing multi-device candidates cannot create a second bootstrap branch.
amendment_note: ADR-0146 makes every request transition out of OPEN terminalize losing RESERVED siblings before key destruction, clarifies reply_route as one logical response with bounded physical use and caps distinct candidates, and binds wrapper expiry to its authority context. ADR-0147 derives the bootstrap deadline from signed route/key expiry, makes candidate accounting non-replenishable, pins replay-only expiry/GC and forbids historical restore of live bootstrap state.

decision: Final bootstrap/resource closure: every MessageRequest transition out of OPEN atomically terminalizes non-winning RESERVED candidates before request-scoped key destruction; acceptance/cancel/decline/expiry/terminal invalidation race on the same OPEN state. reply_route means one logical bootstrap response with exact-wrapper retries and at most 8 distinct admitted candidate wrappers while OPEN. SealedDeliveryEnvelope expiry must not outlive its delivery key, bound route or pending bootstrap request acceptance window, and replay/tombstone retention never extends authority.
amendment_note: ADR-0147 derives the bootstrap deadline from signed route/key expiry, makes candidate accounting non-replenishable, pins replay-only expiry/GC and forbids historical restore of live bootstrap state.

decision: Run-5A normative lifecycle/restore closure: MessageRequest bootstrap_acceptance_deadline is exactly min(reply_route.expires_at, reply_delivery_key.expires_at) with no hidden v1 request expiry; the eight-candidate OPEN budget is durable and non-replenishable; exact winner replay and COMPLETE_REPLAY_ONLY/EXPIRED retention have explicit authenticated deadlines; historical restore cannot reactivate live bootstrap keys/request/replay state; and recovery-alone verifier timers use a crash-safe persisted monotonic elapsed lower bound that wall time/reboot/old backup cannot accelerate.

Run-6A promotes five low-risk foundations into OM V1 without reopening OM-Crypto-v1 or the frozen W0 event body grammar: reference-client multi-IdentityProfile switching; bounded same-profile account-private E2EE draft/selected-preference sync with authority exclusions and concurrent-draft loss protection; optional non-critical om.voice-note.v1 and om.location-card.v1 extensions with W0-safe fallbacks; and owner-root-controlled algorithm-agile/PQ-ready software-release signatures. Live location, SPQR, PQ MLS, stories, cloud scheduled send, payments, mini-apps and other high-cost later features remain deferred.
amendment_note: ADR-0149 schema-registers and object-scopes the promoted extensions, binds location fallback to exact coordinates, adds causal/revocation/restore hardening for account-private sync, immutable ProfileExecutionContext for async work, and role/key/policy-bound update signatures.

decision: Run-7A adversarially hardens the ADR-0148 V1 promotions without expanding kernel authority: presentation extensions are canonical registry/object/criticality/schema tuples with integer-keyed values and exact geo fallback equivalence; account-private sync gains authenticated per-origin causal context, tombstone/delete-wins, future-HLC quarantine, revocation and historical-restore anti-resurrection rules; profile-sensitive async work captures immutable ProfileExecutionContext; and software-update thresholds bind distinct authorized role/key/algorithm/root-policy tuples rather than algorithm tags.

Run 8A promotes three additional low-risk foundations into OM V1 without changing kernel authority: privacy-preserving same-LAN message/file delivery is an optional transport capability using ordinary OM encrypted EventID/session/blob semantics with honest storage-durability state; bounded list presentation uses registered non-critical om.rich-list.v1 over W0-valid paragraph fallbacks; and Android/iOS become explicit V1 reference-family targets while PWA remains the first vertical slice. Automatic LAN discovery is capability-gated, the W0 RichText body grammar remains frozen, and native shells gain no protocol privilege.
amendment_note: ADR-0151 clarifies rich-list validation layers: registered schema violations reject the known extension-containing object; schema-valid reference/nesting/ordinal-presence/fallback failures ignore the whole non-critical enhancement and render W0 RichText.

decision: Run-8B rich-list validation closure: om.rich-list.v1 first obeys ADR-0149 registered-extension object/criticality/schema validation, whose malformed known payload rejects the containing ConversationEvent; only schema-valid list presentation semantics are fail-soft, and any reference/nesting/ordinal-presence/fallback mismatch ignores the entire enhancement and renders authenticated W0 RichText unchanged. Valid ADR-0150 encodings and limits are unchanged.

Run 9A makes the final low-risk V1 scope promotions without changing protocol authority: native desktop joins PWA/Android/iOS as a V1 reference-family target over shared Core/UI/PlatformAdapter semantics; Android wake becomes an explicitly replaceable capability (FCM, UnifiedPush-compatible, persistent encrypted wake/fetch, or none) with no correctness/identity dependency; and local PersonRecord cleanup/export becomes V1 convenience UX with explicit diff/permission and no continuity-authority effect. Remaining crypto/social/ecosystem expansions stay deferred.

Run 9B closes the ADR-0152 stale-wake-retirement overclaim: obsolete registrations are retired where possible and are never fetch/message/account authority; if provider-side deletion cannot be confirmed, residual wake/token/profile-linkage retention is provider/platform-defined unless an enforceable finite lease is explicitly declared, so OM does not invent a universal time bound.

Independent review F-01: ADR-0147 left the verifier runtime segment undefined and gave browsers/PWAs no way to credit time between app sessions, making recovery-alone effectively unreachable for PWA contacts. A runtime segment is one OS boot session on a sleep-inclusive monotonic clock; process_only (web) verifiers under Recommended may add high-water-bounded wall-assisted gap credit and must pass a final authenticated veto sweep; Hardened/Maximum stay strict. Residual clock-advance risk is T-132.

Independent review F-02/F-03: ADR-0151's reject-on-malformed rule for known non-critical extensions made event validity depend on registry version (pre-registration clients accept, post-registration clients reject), violating the Gate-B convergence criterion from the first future registration. Non-critical registrations now ignore object/schema failures; only a wire-criticality mismatch or a critical registration rejects. Presentation extensions bind to the text they were validated against: location cards are create-only, need exactly one canonical point, and are suppressed after an edit removes it; list annotations never carry to another event's text.
amendment_note: Future critical IDs are self-identifying through the V1-reserved om.critical.* prefix, closing T-133 criticality-downgrade convergence.

decision: Independent review F-04..F-08: offline-local LAN delivery had invariants but no wire binding (clear-sender exposure risk, no scope) and moves its binding to new design item A-055, scope local_delivery (W1) and gate V-024, with four architectural rules fixed now; every later-wave gate must freeze its wire objects as CDDL plus two-codec vectors before authorization; scheduled send and implementation-namespaced account-private sync are specified; open design blockers block only the scopes they list, matching RELEASE_WAVES §5.3.
amendment_note: ADR-0157 splits interoperable GroupHistoryBundle from implementation-private DeviceHistorySnapshot and strengthens scheduled-send late binding. ADR-0158 resolves A-055 with the concrete LAN profile.

decision: Independent non-Anthropic review closes three semantic gaps: V1 reserves om.critical.* so unknown future critical extensions reject even if the sender clears the wire bit; implementation-private same-owner history is renamed DeviceHistorySnapshot while interoperable GroupHistoryBundle belongs to the groups wire profile; and scheduled-send queues retain compose intent only, resolving eligibility/fanout/epoch and producing ciphertext only at actual send.

A-055 is design-resolved by LanDeliveryProfile v1: 900-second epochs, K=8 rotating tags, purpose-separated pair/invite rendezvous derivations and seed-encrypted signalling that hides SDP/ICE credentials, ordered reliable WebRTC DataChannel framing with 16 KiB chunks and bounded backpressure, ephemeral om+lan RelayEntry reuse of the frozen sealed-delivery route binding, ordinary SealedDeliveryEnvelope/MLS bytes, unchanged IntroGate/MessageRequest first-contact authority, and transport-neutral BlobID/EventID reconciliation. V-024 remains open for vectors/models/browser evidence/independent review.

The V1 reference-client UX is reconciled around a Chats-first user-composable shell and local-first Omnibar while preserving the full architecture V1 surface. Semantic Action Registry entries map to typed Core intents/PlatformAdapter capabilities rather than generic RPC; local personalization may rank targets but not hidden verbs; recovery/protection/device-control/onboarding semantics follow canonical architecture; OwnMessenger/OhMessenger remain presentation-only safety-bounded layers; detailed UI artifacts live under docs/ux-design; V-018 and V-022 remain open.

Run-2 protocol/security audit makes DeviceID revocation terminal across messaging/control roles; defines branch-tolerant deterministic convergence for hash-chained RelaySet and BlobLocationRecord without changing W0 shapes; binds GroupHistoryBundle to Room/recipient/membership state and makes bundled items inert archive/display material outside live event/control reducers; pins ACS minimum_crypto_profile to the one_to_one security-generation axis while group floors remain Room state; corrects the stale T-133 critical-extension residual. Engineering remains unauthorized.

Run-3 UI hardening, layered on the ADR-0159 Chats-first user-composable shell by ADR-0166: a profile-local recognition-oriented Omnibar with optional user pins; adaptive ranking remains local/profile-isolated and cannot become trust or authority; semantic color/icon roles are explicit (ADR-0159 OM Clear presets supply the seeds); untrusted themes cannot replace semantic action/security icons; theme asset paths/extraction are traversal-safe/bounded; density, motion intensity and alert policy remain explicit user settings; user-pinned visual call participants are not displaced by active-speaker layout. Engineering remains unauthorized.

Run-5 implementation-readiness hardening separates authorization dependencies from integration prerequisites, adds machine-owned per-scope implementation contracts, requires durable stable operation identity plus unknown-outcome reconciliation across crash/network uncertainty, fixes group membership/control changes to a prepared exact-Commit journal with atomic canonical promotion and no tentative-branch messaging, and gives Core/UI provider-neutral outcome/retry semantics. No scope is authorized and no W0 wire field changes.

Run-6 dangerous-algorithm supplement freezes implementation ordering, state transitions, failure handling and forbidden shortcuts for ACS validation, 1:1/sealed delivery, group Commit recovery, mutable reachability convergence, GroupHistoryBundle isolation, extension dispatch, LAN admission and unknown-outcome reconciliation. It adds no wire fields, crypto primitive or engineering authorization.

Run-7 freezes protocol evolution/change control: published IDs and meanings are immutable; profile negotiation is security_generation-first with deterministic equal-generation ID tie-break; extension criticality is immutable and future critical semantics use the reserved om.critical. prefix (ADR-0157); incompatible changes require new profile/extension/object lineage or explicit fork; every normative change uses an explicit strongest-applicable change class and required artifact path; engineering agents receive machine-checkable forbidden-shortcut guardrails. Engineering remains unauthorized.

Consolidate the parallel 2026-09-29 lines: the independent-review/R15-R16C line is the trunk; Run 2-7 ADRs/ledger IDs are renumbered after it (ADR-0161..0165, D-182..186, R-361..386, T-139..155); Run 1's '!'-class, AccountHistorySnapshot and TLS-exporter LAN variants are not adopted in favor of the reviewed ADR-0157/0158; Run 3 becomes a hardening layer on the ADR-0159 shell with the ADR-0159 presets. No gate is passed and engineering remains unauthorized.

Operator directs that Claude performs all remaining reviews. A recorded Claude review pass (written brief, re-executed evidence, adversarial checks, findings with resolutions) satisfies pre-engineering independent_reviewer requirements, labelled pre_engineering_review_basis=operator_single_vendor_ADR-0167; independent_tool/independent_implementation keep their meaning; pre-release and external_review still require humans.

core_kernel review findings: freeze resolution gains normal-mode majority authority (co-signed recovery vote, revocation of non-signers) so one stolen device cannot lock a two-controller account (F-14); V-005 tooling is scoped to the frozen W0 wire and its corpus regenerated (F-15); later-wave enum values such as sig_role 7 are wave-scoped and never widen frozen W0 validity (F-16).

Engineering scope core_kernel (W0) is authorized: all its gates and V-017 have passed pre-engineering phases, cross-wave feasibility is evidenced, no design item blocks it and its conformance suites are specified. Every other scope stays unauthorized; verification prototypes remain evidence and product crates replay the committed vectors.

W0 provider/client review: PR-013 gains a 90% single-vendor-block survivability target for resilience claims (F-18); the performance measurement plan gains sample-size, device-state, clock-offset, fixture, CI-regression and no-release-telemetry controls (F-19); V-018's participant-study criteria move unchanged to its pre-release phase because the study needs the running reference client.

Engineering scope provider_reference (W0) is authorized: it depends only on core_kernel, V-015/V-020/V-022 and V-017 have passed pre-engineering phases, no design item blocks it and its provider conformance suite is specified. The reference provider stays replaceable and never becomes Core authority.

V-006 passes pre-engineering for the first-release web matrix macOS Chrome/Safari/Firefox, iOS Safari and Android Chrome (Windows Chrome/Edge untested and carried pre-release); WebDeviceVault selects its wrapper by an enrollment-time test and states the reduced at-rest property for synced-passkey PRF (R-391); new-origin migration works via the recovery key (R-392); engineering scope reference_client_ui (W0) is authorized under the ADR-0167 review model.

GroupCommitOrdering v1: the canonical successor among valid same-parent Commits is the minimum of (non-reducing, direct, committer DeviceID, binding hash); acceptance is immediate and a losing branch is detected, left and recovered by a roster-neutral, roster-gated re-add or external commit; a removal on a losing branch is not a removal; sequencing_timeout gains a 30-second minimum. Verified by GroupCommit.tla and an OpenMLS 0.9.0 probe on native and wasm32.
